Title: 'LEADING CANONICAL COST WORKED EXAMPLE — "How do I attribute Trino query cost per tenant / per team for chargeback?"'. Key content:
  - The framing problem: Trino on-prem has NO per-query dollar charge; per-tenant attribution = share-of-cluster-work consumed.
  - Three-vector tenant-identification table (`source` / `"user"` / clientTags) with their Trino columns + the client-side setting mechanism (`X-Trino-Source` / `X-Trino-Client-Tags` / JWT `sub`).
  - VERBATIM Step 2 SQL recipe — `JOIN system.runtime.queries q TO system.runtime.tasks t ON q.query_id = t.query_id`, SELECT `q.source`, `COUNT(DISTINCT q.query_id)`, `SUM(t.split_cpu_time_ms)/1000.0`, `SUM(t.physical_input_bytes)/1e9`, plus a `pct_cluster_cpu` window-function column for share-of-cluster normalization.
  - Step 3 optional dollar conversion using the cluster's fixed-annual-cost ÷ vCPU-seconds-available rate.
  - Step 4 event-listener pointer for >15-min windows (durable `QueryCompletedEvent` records with `metadata.queryStats.totalCpuTime`, `context.user`, `context.source`, `context.clientTags`).
  - 9-row DO-NOT-WRITE matrix banning: `tenant_id` column on `system.runtime.queries` (doesn't exist), `cost_usd`/`billed_amount`/`credits` columns (none exist on on-prem Trino), `catalog` column (doesn't exist — search `query` LIKE), `system.runtime.query_stats` (table doesn't exist — JOIN queries+tasks), `peak_memory_bytes` column (doesn't exist — JMX MBeans only), bare `q.user` unquoted (silent wrong-value bug, parses as `current_user` builtin), 30-day window on in-memory `system.runtime.queries` (only ~15 min retention — use event listener), billing by query COUNT (punishes efficient SQL — bill by share-of-cluster-work), and writing INSERT INTO system tables (read-only — persist to your own observability table).
  - Why-this-exists meta-rule + cross-ref chain to r18 (column reference + ephemeral note + event listener setup), r05 (resource groups for per-tenant enforcement), r22 (federation cost attribution).

  **r18 (query-perf-regression) — new LEADING CANONICAL block** inserted between the FIRST 60 SECONDS canonical block and the '## Triage priority order' header. Title: 'LEADING CANONICAL ONCALL TUNING-LEVERS — "Which Trino session properties should I set to speed up a slow query?"'. Key content:
  - The naming rule table: config property (`etc/config.properties`, dots/hyphens, requires restart) vs session property (`SET SESSION ...`, underscores, per-query). Same underlying setting, DIFFERENT spelling. Session form can only LOWER memory-limit caps.
  - Five-lever table (verbatim): `join_distribution_type` (AUTOMATIC/BROADCAST/PARTITIONED), `join_max_broadcast_table_size` (100MB default), `enable_dynamic_filtering` (true default), `query_max_memory_per_node` (30% JVM heap default), `task_concurrency` (node-CPU default, clamped 2-32). Each row: session form (underscores), config form (dots/hyphens), what it does, when to reach for it.
  - Verbatim usage example showing `SET SESSION` syntax + `RESET SESSION` for cleanup.
  - Verification snippet: `SHOW SESSION LIKE 'join_distribution_type'`, `%dynamic_filter%`, `query_max_%`.
  - 10-row DO-NOT-WRITE matrix banning: `SET SESSION query.max-memory-per-node` (config spelling in session statement), `SET SESSION enable-dynamic-filtering` (hyphens), `SET SESSION task.concurrency` (dot), bare `SET <prop>` without SESSION keyword (Postgres/MySQL), invented `join_distribution_type` values like `'HASH'`/`'SHUFFLE'`/`'REPARTITIONED'` (the three valid are `'AUTOMATIC'`/`'BROADCAST'`/`'PARTITIONED'`), bare `dynamic_filtering_wait_timeout` without catalog prefix (system-level master switch is `enable_dynamic_filtering`, NOT a wait-timeout), `/*+ BROADCAST(t) */` combined with `SET SESSION` (Spark/Hive composition — Trino 467 has no hints), `ALTER SESSION SET ...` (Oracle), `SET LOCAL ...` (Postgres transaction-scoped), 'disable DF to speed up query' (almost always wrong — leave DF on).
  - Why-this-exists meta-rule explicitly naming the dot-vs-underscore fab as the #1 Trino-tuning fab class + cross-ref to r24 LEADING CANONICAL join-distribution + r23 anti-patterns + r22 federation per-catalog DF + r27 §4.4B cross-dialect-spillover guardrail.
